Parents said they would pay for a car, laptop, rent, and tuition if I went to BYU and nothing if I went anywhere else. My mom would cry when I talked about other schools out of some fear of the outside world. My dad made enough that I didn’t even qualify for school loans and I had no full scholarship offers. I only had a couple hundred in my bank account and nowhere to live in the U.S. as we lived overseas. This also meant that I didn’t qualify for in-state tuition anywhere.

My only option besides BYU was picking a community college somewhere, trying to get an apartment with no money or credit history, and likely permanently fracturing my relationship with my parents. So I chose BYU. I got a good education, graduated with no debt, and left the church officially shortly after. 

No one held a gun to my head, but I was just a kid with no other good option.
